title: Padres to acquire Robbie Ray from Giants to boost rotation: Source
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

The San Francisco Giants on Monday agreed to trade left-hander Robbie Ray to the San Diego Padres for right-hander Miguel Mendez and shortstop Joniel Hernandez, a league source told The Athletic.

Ray, a impending free agent, would immediately slot atop the Padres’ rotation alongside Michael King. San Diego, desperate for starting pitching and leaning heavily on an expanded bullpen, has carried a temporary two-man rotation of King and Walker Buehler while going 8-1 over the past nine games.

The Giants will take half the money owed to Ray, including half of the $1 million assignment bonus. In return, they get Hernandez, a 17-year-old shortstop from Cuba who got a $1.4 million bonus in January, and Mendez, who was a top-5 prospect in the Padres’ system. Mendez is on the 40-man roster and has dealt with some shoulder issues but could impact the team next season.

Ray is a 34-year-old well-traveled left-hander who had a career season in 2021 for the Toronto Blue Jays when he won a Cy Young Award after leading the American League in ERA (2.84 ERA) and strikeouts (248). He parlayed that season into a five-year, $115 million contract with the Seattle Mariners but gave them just one healthy season before he required a complete surgical reconstruction on his left arm to repair a torn flexor tendon and a torn ulnar collateral ligament.

Ray was in rehab mode when former Giants president of baseball operations Farhan Zaidi acquired him from Seattle for outfielder Mitch Haniger and right-hander Anthony DeSclafani in what was essentially an exchange of underwater contracts. Zaidi was long gone last season when Ray proved to be worth the wait, reestablishing his swing-and-miss high fastball and pitching well enough (9-3, 2.63 ERA in his first 19 starts) to make his second career All-Star team.

Ray hasn’t quite duplicated that stellar first half this season but he was lights out in June when he posted a 1.36 ERA.

Ray rode a fastball-slider combination to his Cy Young season but has reinvented his pitch mix several times with the Giants, first incorporating a changeup that he learned after cold-texting Tarik Skubal for help prior to last season, and more recently, backing off his four-seam fastball while upping the usage of his sinking, two-seamer. He’s also throwing a knuckle curve that held batters to a .125 average through the end of June.

Ray says he wants to keep pitching long enough to be major-league teammates with his 11-year-old son, Asher. As outlandish as that goal might be, Ray’s ability to keep adjusting should allow him to keep pitching through the end of the decade, at least. He’s been to the postseason three times, last with Seattle in 2022, and has made two career starts and four relief appearances. But he didn’t complete five innings in either start and would be viewed as more of a complementary piece than a stud addition to a playoff rotation.
